The bar is high, and that is the point. The greatest perk of being an Atlanian is the quality of the people you get to build with. â¡ What It Feels Like To Work Here You will be given more responsibility than feels comfortable. You will be expected to build, not just manage. You will be asked to move with pace and intensity, think like a founder, and ship like it matters, because it does. Our values The principles that shape how every Atlanian works, decides, and grows. Bias for Action When we see a problem, our first instinct is to solve it; not complain or criticize. We think big and move in small, intentional steps toward our goals. Sometimes even a bold but imperfect decision is better than no decision. Action matters; momentum beats hesitation. Bias for Action Giving 120% & Never Be Satisfied Be Straightforward Problem First, Solution Second One Team From the team In their own words. Pace & Growth "The pace of growth here is unlike anything I've experienced. I've learned more in my time at Atlan than in the previous decade of my career. We operate with real ownership, deep trust, and high standards." Riona Lavin Talent Acquisition Leader, UK Ownership "The work is fun because it's genuinely hard and very real. The culture is what keeps me here. You are trusted with real problems, supported when things break, and surrounded by smart, kind folks." Anbarasan Thangapalam Engineering Leader, India AI-Native Work "I've been at Atlan for over 6 years, solving complex GTM problems alongside some of the sharpest minds in any room. AI is built into how we work, giving us the freedom to rethink problems without limits." Yukti Agarwal Marketing Leader, India What we look for High standards. Low ego. Clarity & First Principles Break down the problem before you build. You break problems down before you pick up tools. You ask why before how, question assumptions others accept, and tie your work to outcomes that actually matter. Your decisions are backed by logic and evidence, not instinct, seniority, or precedent. Agency & Ownership You move before you're asked. You don't wait to be told. When you see a gap, you move. You've shipped things without being asked, improved processes nobody asked you to fix, and taken real accountability for outcomes, including when things went wrong. Growth Mindset Failure is data. Feedback is a gift. You treat failure as data and feedback as a gift. You've made real bets that didn't work and learned something useful from each one. You're more interested in getting better than in being right. AI-First Thinking AI is part of your daily craft. You already use AI to augment and automate work. Not occasionally, not experimentally. You've figured out where it sharpens your thinking and where it cuts your time in half. You treat it as a multiplier, not a shortcut. Intrinsic Motivation Your standard doesn't need an audience. You hold yourself to a standard that doesn't depend on who's watching. You care about craft. You push through the hard parts not because someone set the bar, but because you set it yourself and you don't like leaving things half-done. Others Before Self Customer first. Always. You make the team better by being in it. You share credit, answer questions, pull colleagues up, and make calls with the customer and company ahead of yourself. Customer > company > team > me isn't a phrase here; it's how decisions get made. See roles that match these traits Benefits Top-tier offerings across the globe. Competitive Compensation We benchmark at the top of the market and keep compensation simple: strong base salary, performance-based variable pay, and impact-driven equity. Work from Home Work from where you do your best thinking with top-tier hardware, AI-forward tooling, and a home-office stipend. Learning & Development We treat growth like a product: budgets, coaching, and internal and external learning so you can experiment with new AI tools, deepen your craft, and steadily expand your scope year over year. Team Gatherings We're remote-first, not remote-only: focused offsites, local meetups, and high-signal rituals. Flexible Time Off & Leave Flexible time off and modern leave so you can unplug properly, support yourself and your loved ones, and come back ready to drive impact. Health & Wellness From Day-1 health, dental, vision, and mental health and flexible health stipends. Details by Region Ready to apply? Browse open roles Your interview journey Stages vary by role, but most processes follow this shape. 1 Get-to-Know-You Interview 30â45 min An interview with your Atlan Talent Partner. We cover your background, what you're looking for, and share an honest picture of Atlan's product, culture, and team. 2 Deep Dive with the Hiring Manager 45â60 min A focused look at a small number of real projects you've worked on: your role, the decisions you made, the trade-offs you navigated, and what you learned. Sometimes a future teammate joins. 3 Work Sample or Challenge Varies A short take-home or live working session. The format depends on the role. The goal is always the same: see how you think, utilize AI, communicate, and make judgment calls under realistic conditions. 4 Atlanian Interview 45â60 min An interview with a senior leader or founder about how and why you've invested your time to date, agency, feedback, and what doing the best work of your career looks like. 5 Offer and Decision Varies If it's a strong match, your Talent Partner walks you through the offer: compensation, equity, and country-specific benefits. You'll have space to make the right decision. Also good to know AI Use Guidelines AI is core to how we work at Atlan, and we expect you to use it. But interviews are designed to help us understand you : how you think, what you've built, and how you navigate ambiguity. Used well, AI sharpens that signal. Used poorly, it erases it. Before interviews: use AI freely. Research Atlan, explore the space, pressure-test your ideas, tighten your prep. During live interviews: we want your thinking in real time. By accepting an interview, you're committing to showing up without AI assistance unless we explicitly ask you to use it. For take-homes: AI is fair game unless told otherwise. Use it to brainstorm, prototype, and build. Just be ready to walk us through your choices and why. Ltd., one of the leading Earth Observation (EO) data refinery platforms, has partnered with Kenya Agricultural and Livestock Research Organisation (KALRO) to revolutionize agricultural productivity and resilience in Kenya through the use of advanced satellite data and analytics. This strategic collaboration aims to integrate SatSure’s expertise in Earth observation and artificial intelligence with KALRO’s extensive research capabilities to drive data-driven decision-making in the agriculture sector. The partnership will focus on leveraging satellite imagery, remote sensing, and advanced analytics to provide actionable insights for crop monitoring, yield forecasting, soil health assessment, and climate resilience strategies. Speaking on the partnership, Dhruva Rajan, Chief Revenue Officer at SatSure, stated, “We’re thrilled to collaborate with KALRO in bringing cutting-edge geospatial intelligence to Kenya’s agricultural landscape. This strategic partnership marks a significant step toward enabling data-driven policymaking, strengthening food security, and empowering smallholder farmers with near real-time insights into crop health, weather variability, and sustainable practices” KALRO, a premier institution in agricultural research, is committed to improving agricultural productivity and sustainability in Kenya. Salim Kinyimu, ICT Director at KALRO, commented, “Our partnership with SatSure aligns with our vision of integrating technology into agricultural research and extension services. By harnessing satellite-based analytics, we can better understand climate impacts, optimize resource utilization, and empower farmers with precise, timely information.” Paving the Way for Innovation The MoU between SatSure and KALRO will pave the way for pilot projects, joint research initiatives, and the development of digital tools that support agricultural stakeholders, including government agencies, agribusinesses, and farmers. By combining SatSure’s geospatial intelligence capabilities with KALRO’s on-ground expertise, the collaboration is set to enhance Kenya’s agricultural resilience and contribute to the country’s food security goals. About SatSure SatSure is one of the world’s leading Earth Intelligence companies, delivering analytics-ready data products that enable contextual, industry-specific Earth Observation (EO) solutions at a global scale. It is an end-to-end EO data refinery platform—transforming EO data into decision intelligence—designed to address global challenges across sectors such as Agriculture, Banking, Aviation, Utilities and Critical Infrastructure, and Natural Resources, including Water and Forestry. About KALRO The Kenya Agricultural and Livestock Research Organization (KALRO) is a premier research institution dedicated to enhancing agricultural productivity and rural development in Kenya. KALRO conducts cutting-edge research in crop sciences, livestock management, and sustainable farming practices to support the country’s agricultural sector. You will work directly with leadership, product teams, engineering managers, AI researchers, customers, and business stakeholders to prioritize initiatives, define execution strategies, monitor product health, and ensure timely delivery of enterprise-grade AI solutions. Convert business requirements into well-defined product features and technical deliverables. Own product lifecycle management from ideation to production release. Gather and prioritize customer feedback, market trends, and competitive insights. Define Product Requirement Documents (PRDs), user stories, feature specifications, and acceptance criteria. Prioritize product backlog based on business value, customer impact, and technical feasibility. Drive feature planning for AI products, enterprise platforms, and SaaS offerings. Technical Program Management Lead multiple cross-functional technical programs simultaneously. Own execution of complex AI and software engineering initiatives. Define program goals, milestones, dependencies, and release schedules. Coordinate engineering efforts across backend, frontend, AI, infrastructure, DevOps, and QA teams. Manage interdependencies between multiple engineering workstreams. Identify execution risks early and proactively drive mitigation plans. Ensure alignment between engineering execution and business objectives. Project Management Develop detailed project plans with timelines, deliverables, resource allocation, and milestones. Drive Agile ceremonies including sprint planning, stand-ups, retrospectives, and release planning. Track project progress and remove execution bottlenecks. Manage project scope, timelines, budgets, and stakeholder expectations. Ensure predictable delivery with measurable outcomes. Monitor engineering velocity, sprint health, and delivery metrics. AI & Technical Leadership Partner with Engineering Managers, Architects, Product Managers, and Technical Leads to drive the successful execution of engineering initiatives. Develop a strong understanding of the product architecture, system design, APIs, cloud infrastructure, and software development lifecycle to effectively manage technical programs. Coordinate development across Backend, Frontend, Mobile, AI, DevOps, QA, Security, and Infrastructure teams. Facilitate technical discussions to identify dependencies, risks, implementation strategies, and delivery milestones. Work with engineering teams to estimate effort, prioritize technical debt, and balance feature development with platform stability. Ensure engineering best practices, coding standards, release processes, and quality benchmarks are followed across projects. Monitor technical progress, resolve cross-team blockers, and ensure alignment between engineering execution and business priorities. Support architecture reviews and design discussions by driving decision-making, documentation, and stakeholder alignment without being directly responsible for solution design. Coordinate product releases, production deployments, and post-release monitoring in collaboration with Engineering and DevOps teams. Stay informed about emerging technologies, AI trends, cloud platforms, and enterprise software practices to make informed program and product decisions, without requiring deep hands-on expertise. Cross-Functional Leadership Act as the central point of coordination between Product, Engineering, AI Research, Design, QA, Security, DevOps, Customer Success, Sales, and Leadership. Foster collaboration across distributed technical teams. Drive decision-making through structured discussions and data-backed insights. Facilitate executive reviews and program governance meetings. Customer & Business Engagement Engage with enterprise customers to understand business challenges and product requirements. Translate customer needs into scalable technical solutions. Participate in solution discussions, product demonstrations, and strategic customer meetings. Support pre-sales and post-sales teams during enterprise implementations. Execution & Delivery Excellence Ensure timely delivery of high-quality product releases. Define release plans and deployment strategies. Coordinate UAT, production rollout, and post-release monitoring. Drive continuous improvement in engineering processes. Establish measurable KPIs for product success and engineering efficiency. 0 2 Required Skills & Qualifications Bachelor's degree in Computer Science, Information Technology, Engineering, Electronics, or related field. MBA, M.Tech, or equivalent postgraduate qualification is preferred. Experience working in AI, SaaS, Cloud, Enterprise Software, or Platform Products. Strong understanding of software development lifecycle and Agile product development. Required Competencies Strong technical aptitude with product thinking. Ability to balance customer needs with engineering feasibility. Excellent leadership and stakeholder management skills. Exceptional communication and presentation abilities. Strong analytical and data-driven decision-making skills. Ability to influence without direct authority. High ownership, accountability, and execution focus. Comfortable managing ambiguity in a fast-paced startup environment. Strategic thinker with a bias for action and execution. A LIETF’s prospectus contains its investment objectives, risks, charges, expenses and other important information, and should be carefully considered before investing. In general, a Leveraged ETF is designed to provide a multiple (e.g., two times) of the performance of the index, benchmark or single-security it tracks. An Inverse ETF is designed to provide the opposite of the performance of the index, benchmark or single-security it tracks. A Leveraged Inverse ETF is designed to provide a multiple of the opposite of the performance of the index, benchmark or single-security it tracks. Please keep in mind that LIETFs typically seek to achieve their investment objectives on a daily basis (i.e., over one trading session). When held for longer than one day, the performance of LIETFs can differ significantly from the performance (or the inverse of the performance) of their underlying index, benchmark or single-security over the same time period. This effect can compound the longer the product is held and result in large and unexpected losses, particularly in volatile markets. LIETFs also amplify the volatility and related risk associated with a fund’s underlying index, benchmark or single-security. Volatility refers to the frequency and magnitude of changes in the prices of a financial instrument. Generally, the higher the volatility of an instrument, the greater its price swings and the more risk associated with it. The increased volatility associated with LIETFs may be especially pronounced with respect to funds that provide exposure to a single-security, which by their nature, are not diversified. Further, LIETFs may face liquidity concerns. Liquidity refers to the ability of market participants to buy and sell securities at a competitive price. Greater volatility in LIETFs may lead to market dislocations and higher probability that LIETFs may be restricted from trading or be liquidated. As a result, there may be lower liquidity involving LIETFs, which may result in an investor not being able to sell a LIETF or having to accept a discounted price to do so. This is especially the case for exchange-traded notes (ETNs), which present additional and distinct risks from LIETFs. But why? Vested Shorts: $16B of AI stocks sold overnight, SoftBank used OpenAI shares to buy OpenAI shares, Leverage drove Korean market activity. But why? by Abhishek Sahoo August 9, 2026 6 min read Share Copy link Share on Whatsapp × Table of Contents Toggle The World in a Week: How Major Markets Moved News Stories 5x-bagger fund sold $16B stocks to rival overnight Leverage drove Korean investing activity SoftBank used OpenAI shares to buy OpenAI shares Welcome back to a new edition. On July 27, the American markets show host Jim Cramer told viewers to stop buying AI stocks with borrowed money. He put it simply: “If you’re on margin, get off it. [..] I no longer feel that you’ll get out alive.” On margin means you borrowed to buy the shares. If they fall far enough, your broker could even sell them without asking. Three days after Cramer’s statement, a hedge fund up 439% for the first half of the year was sold out exactly that way, its whole $16 billion portfolio bought by a rival overnight. That same week, 1.2 million small investors in Seoul got the same demand. SoftBank borrowed $10 billion against its OpenAI shares. Borrowed money had a loud week. We’ll get to the interesting bits. But first, let’s see how the rest of the world held up this week. The World in a Week: How Major Markets Moved United States : Markets went up on a bad jobs report. The US shed 23,000 jobs in July against expectations of 83,000 additions , with the previous two months revised down by a combined 103,000 . Unemployment still fell to 4.1% , but only because 264,000 people left the labour force . Participation dropped to 61.4% , its lowest in more than five years. Traders focused on one thing. The Fed’s next move was supposed to be a hike, and a shrinking payroll count makes that harder to justify. Odds of a September increase fell to about 42% from 55% . That was enough. The S&P 500 closed Friday at a record and US stocks had their best week since mid-April , led by chip stocks. The Philadelphia Semiconductor Index rose 9.3% on the week after sliding more than 20% through July. Asia : Shanghai led the region. Japan and India were quieter, both up modestly. Gold hit a seven-week high in the same week, which does not fit a simple rate-relief story. Brent rose above $83 on Friday as Strait of Hormuz tensions flared again. US inflation data lands next week. The tell of the week: a shrinking workforce made a weak jobs report look like good news. News Stories 5x-bagger fund sold $16B stocks to rival overnight On July 24 , Leopold Aschenbrenner wrote to the investors in his hedge fund. He reported a 439% net return for the first half of the year , and added a postscript saying it seemed like a good time to put in more money. “Situational Awareness” is the name of the fund he started in late 2024 after leaving OpenAI, named after a 165-page essay he had written about where AI was heading. It bought the companies building AI hardware, and it bought them with borrowed money, reportedly as much as 4x . The long positions included SK Hynix, Micron , Nebius, SanDisk and CoreWeave . The short positions were in software companies. Unfortunately, both sides went wrong at once. SK Hynix fell almost 50% from its June peak, and the banks that had lent Situational Awareness the money asked for more collateral, meaning cash or assets pledged as security against the loan. The fund did not have it, so something large had to be sold. Citadel, another $71 billion hedge fund run by Ken Griffin, approached late on July 29 and negotiated overnight, outbidding rivals Millennium and Jane Street. Before the opening bell, Citadel bought that pile of AI stocks, worth roughly $16 billion , for more than 10% less than the shares were trading at. Situational Awareness ended July down about 67% , its assets falling from roughly $45 billion in early July to about $10 billion . Sounds more like – Anyways, here is the part worth sitting with. Over the four sessions that followed the sale, the Nasdaq 100 rose 9.3% . Citadel’s flagship Wellington fund had been up just 0.45% for July as of July 24 . It closed the month up 5.9% , its best month since 2022. Anyone who has watched a family sell gold in a hurry knows the price you get is not what the gold is worth. It is what someone will pay you today, because you cannot wait until tomorrow. The buyer on the other side of that counter is not smarter. They are just not in a rush. Here is the detail that makes the point. Even after losing 67% in a month, the fund is still up roughly 80% for the year . Aschenbrenner told investors it will stop borrowing from banks to boost its stock bets. Leverage can actually jeopardize the very advantage it creates. And the coming stories prove the point even further. Leverage drove Korean investing activity On June 19 the KOSPI, South Korea’s main stock index, hit an all-time high of 9,385.59 . By July 29 it closed at 5,663.24, about 40% below that peak, with roughly $2 trillion of market value gone in 40 days. The sessions of July 28 and 29 did most of the damage, wiping out 864.5 trillion won (“won” is South Korea’s currency) between them. The reason was: concentration meeting borrowed money. Samsung Electronics and SK Hynix together are more than half the index. Korean retail investors had been buying both with margin loans and with leveraged ETFs , products that automatically buy more when prices rise and sell when they fall. When prices fell, the “ margin calls ” started. A margin call is your broker telling you the shares you bought with borrowed money have dropped too far, and that you have a short window to put in more cash or they will sell your holdings for you. Goldman Sachs estimated that by July 13, more than 1.2 million Korean accounts had received margin calls, with roughly 320,000 to 360,000 already sold out . Margin loan balances had hit a record 38.63 trillion won on June 24. Then, on July 31, the KOSPI rose 17.91% , its biggest one-day gain ever, after Microsoft’s overnight results beat expectations and calmed fears about AI spending. That day, foreign investors bought a net $5 billion of Korean shares. Korean retail investors sold a record $5.7 billion . Here is what almost nobody is talking about. Americans are borrowing against their shares at a record pace. FINRA, the US brokerage regulator, put total margin debt at $1.502 trillion in June, up 49% from a year earlier . Mind you, it happened with US markets at or near record highs, not during a crash. And like they say, nothing goes wrong while nothing goes wrong. SoftBank used OpenAI shares to buy OpenAI shares On August 5 , alongside its June-quarter results, SoftBank disclosed that it had borrowed $10 billion , pledging its OpenAI shares as security. Goldman Sachs, JPMorgan, Apollo, Mizuho Securities and Sumitomo Mitsui all took part in the loan. The money goes toward the final $10 billion of a $30 billion OpenAI investment it has to pay by October. That will take SoftBank’s total spending on OpenAI to roughly $64.6 billion for about 13% of the company. It has already sold its entire Nvidia stake for $5.83 billion and $12.73 billion of T-Mobile shares to fund earlier tranches, and took a $40 billion bridge loan in March 2026 that comes due in March 2027. Anyways, here is the part worth understanding. Nobody calls this a margin call, because the number has ten zeroes and the borrower wears a suit. But if the assessed value of the OpenAI stake drops far enough, SoftBank has to post cash or give up shares. That is technically what a margin call is. There is one wrinkle. OpenAI is not listed , so there is no daily price for the collateral. The Wall Street Journal reported that banks are normally reluctant to make large loans backed by stock in private, loss-making companies, and that backers of big startups do not usually invest using debt at all. It is like a gold loan where the jeweller’s valuation, not the day’s rate, decides whether you get the call. Anyways, the part that matters for you more is this. Until recently, companies that had not listed yet, like OpenAI, were out of reach for retail investors. That has changed. Private companies like Reflection AI, which builds open-source AI models, and Figure AI, whose humanoid robots ran ten-hour shifts at a BMW plant, are now investable on Vested’s Private Markets . Borrowing against shares hit records in both the US and Korea this year, and Japan’s biggest investor is doing the same, all with markets near highs. Whoever lends you that money picks the day you sell, and it is rarely a good one. So invest what you own, diversify well , and give it time. Thanks for reading! source_text: Our Story, Journey and Philosophy — Kawa Space 0 Skip to Content Products Maritime Domain Awareness SIGINT ELINT Mission as a Service Philosophy Contact Open Menu Close Menu Products Maritime Domain Awareness SIGINT ELINT Mission as a Service Philosophy Contact Open Menu Close Menu Folder: Products Back Maritime Domain Awareness SIGINT ELINT Mission as a Service Philosophy Contact People, Principles, and some House Rules: Among our team are those who have worked on every front of sovereignty and national security. They have launched satellites, flown jetfighters deep into enemy territory and dismantled their camps, commanded war ships, struck deals with militias, led patrols, forged alliances, called for fire, fought wars you’ve heard of — and the ones you haven't. They’ve done the mundane without complaint, and sealed treaties at knife’s edge. Yet, they all converge on the guiding principles for our little project. Principles Don’t feast with people you wouldn't starve with. 初心 nullius en verba. IF. Obsession & hard work > talent. Master the details. Speed matters. Deadlines are sacred. Results count. Money is a measure of results. PO > PR. Space is the next silk route - build roads, not shops. ‘No thanks’ till ‘f**k yes.’ Sovereign individuals only. The only credential check for hiring is: 'Show me what you built.' Work like a Captain, party like a pirate. Make the world dream. Make physics dangerous again. Kawa Space was founded by Kris Nair in March 2019. The plan is to build a critical application and infrastructure layer for the global space industry. This is the third iteration of Kawa Space. Previously we tried a bunch of different things in space data and hardware: We tried building a great software stack, and a wonderful ML stack. It worked for sometime but our horizontal focus didn’t give us enough proof of product market fit. It was heart breaking, but remember all cool cats have many lives. For the last 18 months or so, we have been spending a lot of time with a specific set of customers – this taught us a lot about what they urgently need and how much they’ll pay for it. We are building exactly what they need, we are co-creating the solution with them. They wrote a nice cheque too. Structured FAQ/Feelings. Teams. The teams will be small, each individual owning a key product or feature which matters to our end users. For example, when we ask who is working on ML pipeline for a particular problem set, the answer will be a human name, rather than SDE2, or Chief Architect or CTO. Job Titles. Designations are random. We don’t have titles. You join us as a person, you are defined by the work you do here. "But hey if you don’t have titles, what will I write on LinkedIn?” Write whatever, write CEO if you want or better write what you do, eg: Every day our satellites downlink 260GB of data through our distributed ground stations across the world. Our customers want the metadata of these large datasets ASAP. I along with person A, B and C make the outcome happen in 30 seconds. “ Ok, but I was the Assistant (to) Regional Manager at Dunder Mifflin Sr Vice President of Boeing/Lockheed/ISRO/NASA?” Ok, good for you. Kawa Space is not Dunder Mifflin/Boeing/ISRO/NASA, apples and oranges – you can’t compare. Sovereign individuals. You don’t need a manager. You know what to do. You know what's important. The idea is to co-create something so cool that it makes our past resume-worthy achievements seem like just a blip—and to do it all in style. New People. Our hiring process is a little different. The final question we ask ourselves is: If this person starts a company in the future, would I join them full-time as an employee? If the answer is yes, you're hired. Feel free to show us some proof if you'd like—maybe a funny weekend meme project, some hardware you hacked, or anything else that shows your creativity. No random salary negotiations. For each role, considering an experience bracket & cities we operate from, we have budgets allocated. In your current job you make X , and our bracket is 2X, you get 2X – all humans irrespective of gender or schools attended or companies worked. It's fine to walk in someone else's shoes—as long as they keep them polished. Take the time to listen to smart people with whom you disagree. Forward Deployed Teams. All roles at Kawa Space are forward-deployed engineering roles. Sure, some days you'll enjoy a nice private office. But if your end user is stationed at the national borders or in the middle of a deployment in the Indian Ocean, we go meet them and build things with them right there. This is not for everyone but then we are not looking for everyone. Be Nice. Be nice to each other. Startups are hard, no time, money is tight, a testing instrument costs more than our Series A round etc etc. Read. Strongly urge you to read the following books while you thinking about joining us: Book of Five Rings (Miyamoto Musashi), Skin in the Game (Taleb), the Fabric of Reality (David Deutsch), Interviewing Users (Steve Portigal), Principles (Ray Dalio), Impro: Improvisation and the Theatre* (Keith Johnstone), integral Humanism (Deendayal Upadhyaya) and some more. * yep. Workout, eat well, play a sport with friends. Occasionally sit in silence and meditate. We are a startup. Where Culture Thrives, Careers Soar, and People Come First Connect with us Life at Jash What makes a workplace truly great? It's not just the projects you work on or the technology you build — it's the people, the shared memories, the celebrations that mark milestones big and small, and the culture that holds everyone together. At Jash Data Sciences (JashDS), we believe that an exceptional team culture is the foundation of every great product and every great career. "At JashDS, culture is not a department. It is our identity." Beyond the Office Walls: Annual Team Outings Every year, the JashDS team steps away from screens and sprint boards to spend quality time together in the great outdoors. Our annual team outings have become one of the most anticipated events in our calendar — a tradition that has spanned destinations and memories, growing richer with every passing edition. A Journey Through Our Destinations Each outing is thoughtfully curated to offer a refreshing escape — serene hill stations, resort retreats, adventure parks, and luxury getaways have all been part of our journey. Every destination is chosen to offer something new, ensuring that each outing becomes a chapter in JashDS's story of togetherness. What truly sets our outings apart is that the fun doesn't just happen — it's planned and facilitated by employees themselves. Team games, creative challenges, and collaborative activities are designed and conducted by our own people, fostering a spirit of ownership, coordination, and camaraderie that carries back into the workplace. Runbhoomi: The Annual Sports Festival Every year, JashDS transforms into a sporting arena. Runbhoomi, our flagship annual sports event, is a celebration of energy, team spirit, and healthy competition. Employees come together to participate in a wide variety of indoor and outdoor games — from cricket and football to badminton and beyond. More Than Just Games Runbhoomi isn't just about winning. It's about showing up, cheering for your colleagues, and discovering a side of your teammates you wouldn't see in a conference room. The event fosters genuine bonds, reduces stress, and energizes the entire organization with positivity and enthusiasm. We actively encourage participation in year-round sports activities, believing that active employees are engaged employees. Whether it's a quick cricket match on the weekend or a badminton tournament during Runbhoomi, the playing field at JashDS is always open. Every Milestone is Worth Celebrating At JashDS, we don't wait for annual reviews to make people feel valued. We celebrate every milestone — from work anniversaries and birthdays to personal achievements — because we know that recognition fuels motivation and strengthens belonging. Birthdays & Work Anniversaries Whether it's your first year with the team or your fifth, JashDS ensures that each anniversary is marked with warmth and appreciation. Birthdays are celebrated with heartfelt gestures, and work anniversaries are acknowledged with the recognition that each team member's journey contributes to our collective success. Fun Fridays Fridays at JashDS have a special energy. Our Fun Friday initiative transforms the end of the work week into a canvas for creativity, talent, and laughter. Employees host team games, organize themed activities, showcase personal talents, and plan engaging sessions that bring the entire team together. Fun Fridays are not just events — they are an expression of our team's personality. They remind us that the people we work with are more than colleagues; they are creative, passionate, and wonderfully diverse individuals. CSR at JashDS: Tech with a Heart Great companies don't just create products — they create impact. At Jash Data Sciences, Corporate Social Responsibility is not a checkbox on a compliance form. It is a genuine commitment to the communities around us, driven by the passion of our people. Empowering Blind Students with Career Guidance In another inspiring initiative, JashDS hosted blind students from SP College for an industrial visit at our office. Our leaders guided them through the landscape of career opportunities in the AI and software industry — offering insights, encouragement, and a glimpse into what the future of technology holds. The session was focused on learning, inclusion, and future readiness, embodying our belief that talent knows no barriers. Digital Literacy for the Specially-Abled One of our most meaningful CSR initiatives involved the children of Ayodhya Trust School for the Deaf and Dumb. Our team visited the school to distribute stationery and organize creative activities. But we didn't stop there. Employees volunteered on their weekly offs, visiting in small groups to teach the children the basics of Microsoft Office — Word, Excel, and PowerPoint — and engaging with them to better understand their needs and aspirations. These sessions were as transformative for our team as they were for the students. They deepened our sense of purpose and reminded us of the power of technology to create inclusion. Campus Recruitment: Building Tomorrow's Talent Through our campus recruitment drives, we open our doors to fresh graduates — conducting tests and interviews on campuses, giving young talent the opportunity to begin their careers at the forefront of data science and AI. We don't just hire from campuses; we invest in them. A Culture of Continuous Learning In a field that evolves as rapidly as data science and AI, standing still means falling behind. JashDS is built on a foundation of continuous learning — where curiosity is rewarded, knowledge is shared, and innovation is celebrated. Knowledge Hour & Internal Hackathons Our Knowledge Hour sessions bring the team together to explore new concepts, tools, frameworks, and ideas. These peer-driven learning sessions encourage employees at all levels to share what they know and learn from one another — creating a culture where expertise flows freely across teams. Internal Hackathons take this a step further, challenging our data engineers and scientists to solve real problems under time constraints, with creativity and collaboration as their primary tools. These events have sparked some of our most innovative ideas and produced prototypes that have gone on to influence actual product development. Corporate Trainings & Skill-Up Programs Structured corporate training programs equip our teams with the skills they need to excel in their roles and grow into future leaders. From technical upskilling to soft skills development, JashDS invests in the full professional growth of every employee. Tech Talks & Industry SME Sessions We regularly invite external speakers and industry subject matter experts to share their perspectives through Tech Talks. These sessions bring fresh viewpoints from outside our walls, exposing our teams to cutting-edge developments across AI, data engineering, Industry 4.0, and beyond. We celebrate together — not just as colleagues, but as a community that respects and revels in our shared cultural heritage. Ga

How does digital pathology work? ï¼ Digital pathology transforms traditional glass slides into high-resolution digital images that can be viewed, analyzed, and shared electronically. Technology and Operations Management MBA Student Perspectives Assignments Assignment: RC TOM Challenge 2018 Edit Is SigTuple positioned to disrupt medical diagnostic space in India: Can Data become Doctor? By live4ever Student Posted Nov 13, 2018 Next: H&M Bets Big on Machine-Learning to Survive With AI and machine learning overtaking every facet of millennial industry revolution, Healthcare AI application has far-reaching potential. With advances in image recognition, improvement in robotics, Medical startups are revolutionizing the diagnostic space but are we ready for such a change? Can we allow Data to become Doctor? It is predicted that the advent of AI-related technologies will transform all industries, as electricity did more than 100 years ago [1]. Indeed, AI and machine learning seem to be the hottest technologies in healthcare.Â One challenging space that SigTuple, a Bangalore based startup in India is aiming to disrupt is the medical diagnostics field using data-driven intelligence. SigTupleâs mission is to create a data-driven, machine learned, cloud-based solution for detection and trending of anomalies using deep learning algorithms. It aims to dramatically improve the speed, accuracy, and consistency of various laboratory screening processes by providing smart screening options, which are powered by Artificial Intelligence (âAIâ), better tackle cases with high inter-observer variability and improve the solution efficiency by automating much of the manual process carried out by Physicians. It wants to enable doctors to serve more patients, with fewer errors. Is India an ideal marketplace for AI-based screening processes? The answer would be an astounding yes! Medical diagnosis is broken in India. Thereâs a dearth of qualified professionals to match the vast demand. Facilities in urban areas are crowded and the quality of diagnoses suffers while rural areas donât even get served. Fixing Indiaâs diagnostic woes: According to the World Health Organization (WHO) and the Indian ministry of health, there were a total 10,22,859 doctors registered with the state medical councils or Medical Council of India. Assuming 80% availability, it gives a doctor-population ratio of 0.62:1000 as per current population which is estimated to be of around 1.33 billion [2]. The WHO prescribes a minimum doctor population ratio of 1:1000. To achieve a modest doctor-to-population ratio of 1:1,000, India will need 2.07 million more doctors by 2030 [3], according to a study published in theÂ Indian Journal of Public Health. Pathways to Just Digital Future Watch this tech inequality series featuring scholars, practitioners, & activists Poor regulation and corruption compound these woes:Â As per the Economic Survey 2017-18 tabled in Parliament [4], an analysis of prices of diagnostic tests across various cities in India reveals a huge disparity in the price range as well as average pricing. The government enacted the Clinical Establishments Act, 2010, which prescribes minimum standards for clinical establishments, yet regulatory action for standardization and quality assurance is still mostly on paper, leaving a large number of laboratories unregulated and unaccredited. SigTupleâs value proposition given this Indian context magnifies in amplitude. With its fast, automated services requiring less physician interface and capacity to deliver at fixed cost, SigTuple is positioned to fill this gap. The differentiator in ML comes mainly from the quality and quantity of data that goes into the AI engine. In the healthcare field, the availability of data is not an issue but the format in which it is available is. SigTupleâs solves the first piece of this puzzle by digitizing the slides using a smartphone and a regular microscope. Shonit™- the hardware device completes a peripheral blood smear analyzer solution which automates the routine tasks like differential counts. The smartphone does an auto-scan of the slides. SigTupleâs artificial intelligence (AI) platform Manthana then takes over, learning to classify and tag the visual data [5]. Finally, it generates reports containing differential blood counts, visualizations on various blood metrics and suggestions about any abnormalities. The report can then be reviewed by pathologists on any net connected device even remotely and sign off on reports â a massive step to bringing diagnostic access to remote parts of the country. The fact that it not only churns out results but also supports it with visual evidence makes it easily verifiable. The process flow of this operation can be seen below. But first and foremost challenge I see for SigTuple is to convince pathologists across the country on the adaptability of its product. It has to not only build a trusted network of partnerships with hospitals, labs but also overcome the prejudice against any change in the way traditional diagnosis works. Secondly, SigTuple heavily depends on the performance of its hardware component as a starting point to the whole AI process. SigTuple is currently not set up as a hardware manufacturing company. The org structure is heavily focused on the AI domain and medical expertise but it soon needs to attract supply chain and manufacturing talents to ramp up and scale given its latest series B funding raising its investment to $24.8M [6]. Finally, as with all healthcare companies that eventually want to climb up the healthcare pyramid, going beyond screening and diagnosis to offer preventive advice, the nature of the intelligence it generates will get more intimate and the potential legal and ethical implications will get more complex. What steps if any Sigtuple can take to ensure it doesnât become another Theranos in the history of healthcare innovation? And the deeper ethical question comes forefront in mind such as Can Shonit replace human pathologists completely? Can Data in future become a Doctor? November 15, 2018 Don Johnson says: Very interest article. My key concern going forward relating to the application of machine learning in healthcare diagnostics is that: who bears the liability of malpractice relating to sub-standard diagnoses and the associated negative health outcomes? I see this as one of the key roadblocks to widespread adoption because healthcare providers will be reluctant to fully automatic the diagnostic process without 100% certainty that there is no chance of error in the AI-driven process. I fear AI will be limited to a supporting role in diagnostics for the foreseeable future. Which raises the question: what is the real value add versus current methods of diagnosis? November 15, 2018 panda says: SigTuple is trying to solve an interesting problem in the Indian healthcare context. I like the idea of digitizing the slides, but given the poor quality of infrastructure and training in India, who will control the quality of slides being prepared? How will SigTuple ensure that the remotely collected slides confer to the basic quality requirements? I am alluding to the data being fed to the intelligent systems here, and that is really an issue to be thought about while looking at a scalable solution. Comments are closed. Hevo Data - Talent Acquisition Manager Talent Acquisition Manager Bangalore, India BizOps – BizOps / Full time / On-site apply for this job Read this first Most TA manager jobs are about keeping the machine running. This one is about building the machine. If you want a role where the process is already built and you just run it, this is not the one. If you want to build the operating system that brings the best engineering and GTM talent in the country to Hevo, and gives them the best hiring experience of their careers, keep reading. Here is the honest picture. We hire strong people. Our product is trusted by companies like DoorDash, Shopify, and Postman. Our Glassdoor sits at a healthy 4.1, and our team is talented and hungry. The machine works. Now we get to make it exceptional. That is the opportunity. Today a lot of what makes hiring work at Hevo runs on the strength of our people. The job is to build the system underneath them so the excellence compounds and scales with us. That means every candidate hears back faster than they expect. It means every brilliant person our CEO reaches out to on LinkedIn gets a clean, closed loop from the team. It means stakeholders get crisp written visibility, not just a good update on a call. And it means the whole team pitches Hevo the way our best people already do. Nobody has yet owned turning TA into a well oiled machine, and that is exactly what makes this one of the most exciting building jobs in the company right now. What you will actually own 1. Closing the roles that matter, on time, every week. You own the outcome, not the activity. Priorities shift week to week, so every recruiter always knows their top three and is filling those funnels with candidates good enough to convert. When a loop stalls, you unblock it before the candidate cools off. The measure is simple: are the right roles closing, and closing fast. 2. Making our hiring process the best one a candidate runs all year. Great candidates are interviewing at four places, not one, and we win on respect as much as brand. A status update lands within a fixed window at every stage, nobody chases us, and every loop closes with a clear next step or an honest no, including the ones the CEO sources himself. You will see it in our offer accept rate. 3. Giving the business sharp, written visibility into hiring. We are good on a call and weak on paper. You fix that with one standard written update per function each week: pipeline, conversion, time to close, and roles at risk. Leaders read it async and know exactly where things stand. Numbers, not vibes. 4. Building a team that sells Hevo and runs a clean process. You inherit a talented team that has never had a real training path, and you build one: how to tell the Hevo story, screen with judgment, and run a tight loop end to end. The goal is to lift the whole floor, so selling Hevo is something everyone does well, not one person. 5. Turning all of this into a repeatable system. None of this is a one-time cleanup. You codify it, sourcing to offer, into SOPs on the Hevo hiring framework, and own the employer branding fundamentals: Glassdoor, our LinkedIn presence, and the collateral candidates actually see. What the first year looks like Month 1 to 2: You know every open role, every recruiter's strengths, and exactly where the funnel leaks. The candidate communication SLA is live and enforced. The CEO's LinkedIn candidates never fall through the cracks again. Month 3 to 6: The weekly written update is a habit stakeholders rely on. Time to close is trending down on priority roles. The team's training path is built and running. Month 6 to 12: TA runs like a system, not a scramble. The process is documented, the team sells Hevo with confidence, and our candidate experience is something people mention in interviews at other companies. Who you are You have 8 to 11 years in recruiting, with at least 2 to 3 spent managing recruiters or owning a hiring vertical end to end. You have hired across both engineering and GTM. Not one or the other. SDE roles and AE, SDR, SE roles are both familiar territory. You have built or genuinely upgraded a hiring process before, not just executed someone else's playbook. You come from a place with a high hiring bar, ideally a high growth B2B SaaS or product company. You write clearly and you enjoy it. Given where the team is today, this one is non-negotiable. You know the India talent market and the tools we live in: LinkedIn, Instahyre, IIMJobs. Who this is not for If you need a fully built process handed to you, you will find this messy. The mess is the opportunity, but you have to want it. If you avoid hard conversations with hiring managers or with your own team, the accountability part of this role will wear you down. If you would rather report progress on a call than write it down, we are not going to fit. Why Hevo We are building a category-defining data product from India, for the world. Backed by Sequoia, Chiratae, and Qualgro, with over 2,000 customers across 40+ countries and hyper-growth ahead. The talent you bring in over the next two years is the talent that builds that future. Very few roles tie hiring this directly to the outcome of the company. This is one of them. If this sounds like the job you have been waiting to build, we should talk. Hevo has something different. Something that took eight years to build and can't be bought. Over 2,000 companies send us their most sensitive data every single day. 100 billion events a month. Raw. Unfiltered. Before transformation, before aggregation, at the exact moment truth is created. That's not a product feature. That's trust, earned one customer at a time, over eight years, by not screwing up. That position is now the foundation for something much bigger. We're building an Intelligence Layer on top of it, a system that reads across every data source a company runs, connects the signals that matter, and tells people what to do before they have to go looking for answers. We call it the Context Graph. It's real enough to show results. Early enough that the person who joins now defines what it becomes. This is the moment. Not the moment after it's obvious. Now. What You're Walking Into You'll own a product pod. SaaS integrations, database connectors, or the Intelligence Layer, depending on where the biggest need is when you join. You own the backlog. More importantly, you own the why behind everything that gets built. You report directly to the CEO. In the first 3-6 months, your job is to make the foundation bulletproof, find the gaps in the platform, close them, and make the product sharper than it's ever been. After that, you move into the Intelligence Layer and help define what Hevo becomes in its next chapter. What This Job Actually Is Let's be honest about what great PMs do, and what mediocre ones do instead. Mediocre PMs write specs and hand them off. They synthesize feedback from CSMs and call it customer insight. They sit in architecture meetings and nod. They measure their own output in documents shipped, not outcomes delivered. That's not this job. This job is three things, done well, simultneously. First: technical ownership. You will be in the room when architecture decisions get made. Not watching. Contributing. Pushing back. Asking the questions that change the direction of the decision. You need to understand how data pipelines work at a systems level, CDC, connectors, streaming, schema management, failure modes. If you can't hold your own in that room, engineering will stop inviting you to it. And they'll be right to. Second: direct customer engagement. You talk to customers yourself. No intermediary. No secondhand summary. You hear the problem in the customer's own words, you sit with the complexity of it, and you own the translation into product decisions. If you're relying on a CSM to tell you what customers need, you will always be one step behind. Third: making complexity simple. Hevo's product is deeply technical. The people who sell it and support it are not always. A big part of your job is taking complex system behavior and making it crisp and understandable, for Support, for CS, for Solutions Engineering, so they can represent the product confidently to customers. If internal teams are confused, customers will be too. Who We're Looking For 6-8 years of product experience. Meaningful time on platform or infrastructure products at B2B companies. Not optional. Strong technical depth. CS degree or equivalent engineering background. You should be able to hold a real conversation about system design, data architecture, API design, and engineering tradeoffs, not a surface level one. Proven ability to engage directly with customers. Not customer research. Not user interviews handed to you by a researcher. Direct engagement, gathering requirements, presenting product direction, handling objections in real time. Clear, structured communication. Written and verbal. You can make a complex system understandable to a non-technical audience without sacrificing accuracy. This is rarer than it sounds. High ownership. You don't wait for conditions to be perfect. You move. You iterate. You follow through. When you say you'll do something, it gets done. Nice to have: Engineer-turned-PM. Experience at a Series A-C company where you had to balance speed with quality. Familiarity with the data integration and pipeline landscape. Identified and closed the most critical gaps in their product area, with improvements that customers and internal teams can actually feel. Built enough technical depth to shape architecture decisions, not observe them. Become the person in the company most connected to what customers actually need from their product area. Made internal teams measurably better at representing the product. Started actively shaping the Intelligence Layer, contributing product thinking and customer insight as Hevo moves into its next chapter. The Moment Hevo spent eight years building both a product and a business simultaneously, and the foundation is real. The Intelligence Layer is early. The window to define what it becomes is open right now. Most people will look at this moment in five years and wish they'd been here for it. Hevo Data - Strategy & Ops (Founder's Office) Strategy & Ops (Founder's Office) Bangalore, India Strategy – Strategy All / On-site apply for this job Read this part first Experience: 2 to 8 years Location: HSR Layout, BLR Most Strategy and Operations roles quietly turn into reporting jobs. You pull the numbers, format the decks, and remind people about deadlines. This is not that role. This is the role for someone who wants to learn, at close range, how a fast growing company actually plans, prioritizes, and executes. You will work directly with the CEO and the leadership team on the problems that cut across functions, the ones no single team can solve alone. Your job is to turn ambiguity into a plan, and a plan into results. For the right person, this also happens to be one of the best leadership educations available anywhere. People who do this job well at Hevo build the instincts of a real operator, and many go on to run things. But the simplest reason to take it is this: you get to work on what matters most, alongside the people who decide it. What you will own: 1. The operational rhythm of the whole company. You will work with the CEO to keep the entire machine moving across Sales, Marketing, Finance, Engineering, HR, Solutions, and Support. You will run the OKR process with the leadership team, drive quarterly planning and goal setting, and track delivery so nothing important slips. You will be the person who can tell, on any given day, how healthy the organization really is and where attention is needed next. 2. The strategic projects that move the needle. You will partner with the CEO and other leaders to spot the initiatives that genuinely change the trajectory of the business, then own them end to end until they are big enough to stand on their own and get handed to a dedicated team. These are the bets that matter most, and you will be trusted to carry them. 3. Cross functional execution and alignment. You will be the connective tissue across functions, driving communication so the company moves as one. You will be a real thought partner to leadership on vision, priorities, and the hard tradeoffs. You will manage relationships with stakeholders inside and outside the company, and when needed, represent leadership in reviews. Why this role is special: Three things make this seat genuinely rare. You get the full view. Most people spend a decade seeing one function. You will see all of them at once, from the vantage point of the executive team, inside a company growing fast enough to teach you something new every week. You work on first of a kind problems. Nearly every problem you solve will be one you have not solved before. There is no playbook handed to you. You build the playbook. For the right person, that is the most fun part of the job. You build an operator's judgment. Custodian of rhythm, owner of strategic projects, thought partner to leadership. That is the exact muscle set strong operators and founders are made of. You will leave this role with judgment most people take many more years to develop. What you will need to bring: We hire for abilities first, because knowledge and skills can be taught and abilities are far harder to build. Here is what we are really looking for. 1. Stakeholder management. You build trust with people at every level and quickly read what actually drives them. People want to work with you, and they tell you the truth. 2. People leadership. You understand what good leadership looks like up close. You know how to find the right levers and use them to bring out strong performance, and you have nudged teams into action in a way that energized them. 3. First principles problem solving. You are sharp with data, analytics, and reasoning. You break unfamiliar problems down to their fundamentals and build your way back up to a clear answer. 4. Ownership. You take a problem and you get it solved, full stop. You enjoy the wins, you own the misses, and you fix them. High accountability, no excuses. 5. Outwork and outsmart. You bring operational rigour and intensity. You find the smarter path, and you also do the work. 6. Independent thinking. You form your own point of view from the inputs in front of you, build conviction, and have the courage to make the call. 7. High agency. You move things forward mostly through influence, rarely through authority. You align people around the company wide goal by convincing them, not commanding them. Who tends to thrive here: The people who do exceptionally well in this seat usually share a pattern. They are intensely curious about how businesses work. They are comfortable being thrown into something they have never done and figuring it out. They care more about the outcome than the credit. And they have the energy to keep going when a problem turns out to be harder than it first looked, because that is usually where the most interesting work begins.
